name: Messina
title: Messina Ship UTM | Strait Ferry & Repair Yard Gauging
description: Thickness gauging in Messina for Strait ferries, hydrofoils, ro-ro and cargo ships: drydock hull readings, pre-docking steel estimates and alongside surveys.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships at Messina and the Strait
intro: Messina sits on the narrow Strait between Sicily and Calabria, where car ferries cross every few minutes and cargo and passenger ships pass through all day. It also has a repair yard with graving docks. Atlantis NDT brings a thickness gauging team from India to work in dock or alongside, shaped around the yard programme or the timetable of whichever ferry or cargo ship needs the readings.
keywords: strait of messina ferry hull gauging

highlights.h: A graving dock on the Strait
highlights.p: Messina has an established repair yard with graving docks, so ships can be gauged in dry condition during a docking, with full access to the bottom shell, sea chests and stern structure.

highlights.h: Ferries that cross all day, every day
highlights.p: Car ferries working the short crossing to the mainland run an intensive schedule and need planned lay-up to be gauged. Their hulls take heavy use, which makes thorough readings worthwhile.

highlights.h: Strong tidal streams in the Strait
highlights.p: Currents reverse through the Strait and affect how ships approach and lie at berths. Gauging alongside needs the master's agreement on mooring and access, particularly on small craft.

port.h: The port of Messina, the Strait crossing and its mixed traffic
p: Messina occupies the northeastern tip of Sicily, where the Strait narrows to a few kilometres and the Calabrian coast is visible across the water. The harbour is a natural sickle-shaped basin on the Sicilian side, sheltered from the open sea, and the port belongs to the Strait port authority system that also includes Milazzo and the Calabrian ports of Reggio and Villa San Giovanni. The approach is shaped by the Strait itself: tidal streams run strongly and change direction, and the current affects the way larger ships turn and moor at the berths.

Traffic here is a mix of very different ships. The best known is the car-ferry shuttle across to Villa San Giovanni and Reggio, which runs round the clock and carries vehicles, trains and passengers. Hydrofoils and fast craft link Messina with Reggio and the Aeolian Islands, ro-ro ships serve the mainland ports and cruise ships call at the passenger terminal. In the commercial harbour, general cargo ships and tankers load and unload, and the Strait carries a large through traffic of merchant ships that do not call at all. For thickness gauging, the Strait ferries and fast craft are the most persistent source of work.

The crossing vessels operate under pressure. A shuttle ferry makes many more crossings in a year than an overnight ro-pax, with repeated berthing, ramp use and turning in strong current, and it has few quiet seasons. Owners balance that with planned dockings, often in the shipyard in Messina itself, where hull, ramp and tank structure are inspected in dry condition. The hydrofoils and fast craft, many of aluminium, add another kind of work, since they need an aluminium-calibrated gauge and attention to fatigue and corrosion in different places from steel hulls. Messina therefore combines a heavy ferry workload with the facilities to repair ships on the spot.

facilities.h: Where ships can be gauged in Messina
p: The principal facility is the repair yard on the Messina waterfront, part of an established Mediterranean repair group, with graving docks used for dockings, hull repairs and conversions on cargo ships, passenger ships and ferries. During a docking the gauging team works to the yard's programme, taking readings of the bottom shell, sea chests, rudder and stern structure and cleaned tanks before blasting, so that original surfaces are measured. The results feed the steel renewal list agreed between the owner, the yard and the class surveyor in the first days of the docking.

Afloat gauging takes place at the ferry berths and the commercial quays. A Strait ferry laid by for planned maintenance can be gauged in blocks across the lay-by period, while hydrofoils and fast craft are measured during winter lay-up. The naval arsenal and other restricted areas are outside commercial access. Ships at anchor in the Strait are difficult to reach because of the currents and shipping lanes, so anchorage work is limited and depends on a launch and a suitable weather and tide window. Milazzo and the Calabrian ports can be added to one mobilisation by road and ferry.
list: Messina repair yard graving docks — full hull, sea chest, rudder and stern structure gauging during dockings of ferries, cargo ships and passenger ships
Yard repair quays — afloat gauging of tanks, decks and internal structure during refit work before and after undocking
Strait ferry berths — car-ferry hull, ramp and tank readings taken over successive lay-by periods in the shuttle schedule
Hydrofoil and fast-craft berths — aluminium and steel hull gauging with a gauge calibrated for the alloy, mostly in winter lay-up
Commercial quays — general cargo ships and tankers gauged between cargo operations
Passenger terminal — cruise ships gauged during short turnarounds, mainly void spaces and scrubber lines

context.h: Strait regulations, port state control and ferry structure
p: Messina follows the Paris MoU port state control system, with inspections carried out by the Italian Coast Guard, the Guardia Costiera. Passenger ferries and high-speed craft in scheduled service are also covered by the EU's dedicated inspection regime, so structural condition on a Strait ferry gets close attention. The Strait itself is a busy, regulated waterway with traffic separation and mandatory reporting for ships transiting it, and the crossing ferries share it with long-haul merchant traffic; hull damage from contact at berth or in strong current is a real risk, and thickness readings help separate real damage from old wastage.

EU rules add further drivers. The Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials for ships calling at EU ports, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime apply to larger vessels. For the crossing ferries, many of which are older tonnage working intense schedules, the decision whether to renew steel, convert or replace a ship rests on measured condition, and docking records from the Messina yard are the natural starting point. Aluminium craft raise their own checks, since corrosion at joints and in wet spaces differs from steel wastage.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Messina
jobs.p: Messina offers two kinds of work. In the repair yard, we gauge ships in dock to the docking programme, producing readings that feed the renewal list. Elsewhere in the port, we gauge ferries and fast craft during lay-by, building up a picture block by block around the timetable. We agree the sequence with the superintendent, keep to the measurement points the surveyor expects and deliver a single consolidated record at the end.
list: Full hull gauging of a car ferry in a Messina graving dock, covering bottom shell, sea chests, ramp structure and ballast tanks, with renewal areas marked for the yard
Pre-docking readings on a Strait shuttle ferry during planned lay-by, spread over several periods and compiled into a steel estimate
Aluminium hull and frame gauging on a hydrofoil during winter lay-up, using a gauge calibrated on a reference block of the hull alloy
Cargo hold and hatch cover gauging on a general cargo ship at a commercial quay between cargo operations
Owner's condition gauging of a ship at the Messina berths before a charter change or sale

logistics: Reggio Calabria and Catania airports are the nearest gateways and each is reached by road, with Naples and Palermo offering wider connections. Access to the repair yard is arranged through the owner or the yard, and the ship's agent arranges ISPS passes for the ferry and commercial berths. The team travels from India and needs Schengen visas, so dates should be confirmed early; dockings are usually booked well ahead, while ferry lay-by work needs the operator's schedule as soon as it is known.
vessels: Ships in drydock for repair or conversion

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship in dock at the Messina repair yard?
faqs.a: Yes, as a contractor to the owner and under the yard's site rules. The owner or yard arranges access and induction, and we coordinate with the docking planner so the bottom shell and tanks are measured before blasting, with results ready when the surveyor and owner agree the renewal list.

faqs.q: How do you gauge a Strait ferry that runs all day?
faqs.a: In blocks, during planned lay-by or maintenance periods. A ramp, a deck section or a group of ballast tanks is measured each time, and the readings join up across several visits into one report. The superintendent and master decide the order so the crossing schedule is not affected.

faqs.q: Do you measure aluminium hydrofoils at Messina?
faqs.a: Yes. Thickness gauges measure aluminium once calibrated for the alloy, and we calibrate on a reference block of the same material. Fast craft tend to corrode at joints and in wet bilges, so we agree the measurement points with the superintendent and the surveyor first.

faqs.q: Do tidal streams in the Strait affect gauging at Messina?
faqs.a: Mainly the way a ship lies and the access to it. Alongside at a berth, gauging is largely unaffected, but at anchorage or on small craft the current and traffic limit what is practical. We discuss mooring and access with the master and agent before deciding where to work.

faqs.q: Can you cover Gioia Tauro or Milazzo from Messina?
faqs.a: Yes, both are reachable by road, and the Strait ports are close. If an owner has ships at Messina and another port in the same week, we plan one mobilisation, sequenced by each ship's schedule and the scope agreed with its superintendent.
